findings.reason: the section should say it carries an already-parsed field, so a worker does not add a second parser and the interface delta is stated honestly.
findings.text: §3 states the record "gains `skipped` and `skipped_ids`, parsed from the same pytest output it already reads", but the count is already produced: `_result_counts()` maps the `skipped` token via `_RESULT_WORDS` (reckon/crew/standing_suite.py:102) and `_build_counts()` (reckon/crew/standing_suite.py:285) computes `results = _result_counts(...)` then drops `results["skipped"]` when building its return dict. Only carrying that already-computed value into `_build_counts`/`_build_record` (standing_suite.py:253) is new for the count; the plan cites neither function.

findings.reason: naming the existing extractor turns a new parser into a small extension, which is the reuse census this item exists to force.
findings.text: §3's `skipped_ids` should extend the existing per-id extractor `_pytest_failure_ids` (already used to populate `failure_ids` at standing_suite.py:335) rather than introduce a parallel SKIPPED-line parser; the plan names no such reuse. The census of pytest-log parsers in this owner is: `_result_counts` (standing_suite.py:164), `_pytest_failure_ids` (standing_suite.py:335), and the shared `_RUNNER_SUMMARY` (promotion_evidence.py:1000) — the last is already reused and only the middle is unmentioned.

findings.reason: a `helpers/` package is a defensible consolidation and the author may prefer it to the flat layout; this is a placement note, not a design change.
findings.text: §4 introduces a new `tests/helpers/` package without noting the established shared-test-module convention: six non-test modules already live flat at tests/ root (`tests/spa_browser_harness.py`, `tests/spa_containment_harness.py`, `tests/spa_module_eval.py`, `tests/spa_parity_harness.py`, `tests/fleet_supervisor_requests.py`, `tests/mcp_family_reload.py`), and no `tests/helpers/` directory exists today.

findings.reason: the mismatch sits in §1's cited health-review figure, not in §4's gate, which recomputes before/after sums; worth reconciling the citation but it does not change the design.
findings.text: §1's table records `config_home` as "20 each across 5 files", but the §4 done-when's own command `grep -rlE "^def <name>\(" tests/` at HEAD yields a different census: `config_home` 12 files, `_spawn_runner` 5, `_row` 39, `checkout` 8, `_placed_backend` 5, `_replace_stream` 3.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §2 extends the single existing resolver `installed_browser()` (tests/spa_browser_harness.py:532), hiding the resolution order behind it; §4 consolidates 202 clone pairs into subject modules rather than layering wrappers over them; nothing new here spreads shallow surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — no shared mechanism is forked: §3 reuses the shared runner-summary parser `_RUNNER_SUMMARY` (reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py:1000, imported at standing_suite.py:46), §2 extends the sole browser resolver, and §5 rewrites call sites rather than adding an owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1626, cli_options 351, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; no section adds to any of the four families (§2 adds an env var, §3 adds record data fields), so nothing needs a retire/merge justification.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3's skip *count* and per-id extraction already exist inside `reckon/crew/standing_suite.py` and the plan cites neither, presenting already-parsed data as new machinery.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §2 and §3 extend the mechanisms they name (the browser resolver, the suite-record writer) rather than wrapping them, and each states the existing function it changes.
